title: What Drives Demand for Playlists on Spotify?
eligible_reason: The TWFE regressions (analysis/code/loglog-regressions.R) include two simultaneous non-absorbing treatments, any_promo (playlist featured on Spotify's Search Page that day; switches on and off repeatedly) and has_superstar (playlist contains a song by an exceptionally popular major-label artist; switches on and off), together with a long list of time-varying controls (category recommendation intensity, major-label share, playlist duration, track age, nine audio features, and 30 competitor promo/superstar variables) in every column, with playlist (or playlist-by-calendar-month) and date fixed effects. The paper's second main method is a staggered synthetic difference-in-differences (synthdid). Non-absorbing multi-treatment regressions with time-varying controls and synthetic DiD are all excluded by the protocol.
design_notes: Daily panel of 30,000+ popular Spotify playlists, 150 days per playlist (Oct 2019 - Mar 2020), estimation sample nointerpolations_panel = panels with metadata_stretch_length >= 100 and qualifying_stretch_length >= 28, excluding 2019 year-end top playlists. Formula form_fes_ols: log(followers+1) ~ any_promo + has_superstar + log(1+rec_intensity_cat) + log_ml_share_log1 + log(playlist_duration_h+1) + log(wnplaylists_trackage_year+1) + audio features + any_promo_comp1..15 + has_superstar_comp1..15; fixef = c('id','date') or c('id_month','date'); vcov = 'twoway'. Robustness: IHS transform, first-time superstar treatment only (switchcount <= 1), excluding other seasonal promotions. Synthetic DiD module (synthetic_did.R, aggregate_synthdid.R, build_balanced_panels.R) with matched control pools (controlsize 2500, 200 replications).
n_adoption_cohorts_note: Featuring events occur on many distinct days, but the treatment is not absorbing (playlists are featured and un-featured repeatedly), so a cohort count is not meaningful.

specs.exclusion_reason: non-absorbing treatment (featuring switches on/off); second simultaneous treatment (has_superstar); time-varying controls in every column
specs.controls: log(1+rec_intensity_cat), log_ml_share_log1, log(playlist_duration_h+1), log(wnplaylists_trackage_year+1), 9 audio features, any_promo_comp1-15, has_superstar_comp1-15
specs.sample_condition: nointerpolations_panel; robustness subsets switchcount<=1 and other_seasonal==F

data_files_note: The downloaded archive contains code, LaTeX sources, reporting output and 200-byte .txt placeholders for all raw/derived data ('This file replaces the original file ... marked as confidential'). The Dataverse manifest (docs/files_in_repository.csv) lists analysis/temp/panel.csv (4.3 GB, split in two parts), promotions.csv, playlists.csv, playlist-categories.csv, placements-selected-only.csv, top_artists*.csv as available analysis-stage files, but none of them is in the extracted package.
software_note: R 4.3 (data.table, fixest, synthdid, modelsummary), Python 3, GNU Make pipeline
screener_notes: Not a staggered-adoption DiD in the protocol's sense: on/off featuring exposure with a second on/off treatment and rich daily controls, plus synthetic DiD. Even the analysis-stage panel would have to be fetched separately from Dataverse.
